title: A small plan
en: Before I start work, I write down three important tasks. I do not try to plan every minute. A show may finish late, or a teammate may need help. A short list gives me direction without making the day feel crowded. When a task is complete, I mark it and move on. At the end of the day, I can see what I actually did and choose one thing to improve tomorrow.
cn: 工作前我写下三项重要任务，不安排每一分钟，给临时变化留空间。完成一项就做标记，收工时看看实际完成了什么，再选一件明天改进的事。

title: Before the show
en: Our team arrives at the studio before the show. First, we check the camera and the lights. Then we test the sound with a short conversation. One person reads the schedule while another checks the screen. If something looks wrong, we fix it before the audience arrives. This simple routine takes only a few minutes, but it helps everyone feel more prepared. We can focus on the performance instead of worrying about small technical problems.
cn: 开播前，团队检查相机、灯光、声音、时间表和屏幕，提前解决问题。这几分钟的例行检查能让大家更安心地投入表演。

title: A useful break
en: After a busy hour, I put down my phone and take a short break. I get some water and look away from the screen. Sometimes I walk around the room and talk to a teammate. I do not need an exciting activity to feel better. A few quiet minutes can be enough. When I return to work, I read the next task carefully. The break helps me notice details that I missed when I was rushing.
cn: 忙碌一小时后，我放下手机、喝水、看看别处，偶尔走动或与同事聊聊。短暂安静的休息让我回来后更容易注意到赶时间时遗漏的细节。

title: Learning on a busy day
en: Some days are too busy for a long English lesson. On those days, I study five words and say one sentence aloud. I read the example first and try to connect it with my own work. Later, I review the words that were difficult. The lesson is small, but it gives me another chance to practise. I do not wait for a perfect free afternoon. I use the little time that is available today.
cn: 忙的时候，我只学五个单词、大声说一句话，把例句与自己的工作联系起来，再复习难词。不等一个完美的空闲下午，利用今天已有的一点时间。

title: Keeping receipts
en: Last week, I bought train tickets for our team. I paid with my own money, so I kept the receipt and wrote down the amount. At home, I took a clear photo of the ticket and saved it with the record. I also noted who needed to approve the payment. Now I can see which costs are still waiting. When the money arrives, I will add the payment date and close the record.
cn: 上周我替团队买车票，保留凭证并记录金额，拍照后与记录放在一起，也记下需要谁审批。这样能看清待处理费用，到账后再记录日期并结束流程。

title: At the gym
en: I used to walk into the gym without a clear plan. I would choose a machine and guess how much weight to use. Now I check my last record before each exercise. I can see the weight, the number of sets, and how the movement felt. The record does not make the decision for me, but it gives me a useful starting point. I can adjust the session to match how I feel today.
cn: 过去我训练前没有计划，随意选器械和重量。现在先看上次的重量、组数和感受。记录提供参考，今天的安排仍由我结合状态调整。

title: A clear message
en: A good work message does not have to be long. It should tell the reader what happened and what needs to happen next. If a task is unfinished, I explain the reason in a simple sentence. If I need help, I say exactly what kind of help I need. Before sending the message, I read it once more. I remove repeated information and check the dates. A clear message saves time for the whole team.
cn: 工作消息不必很长，说明发生了什么、下一步是什么即可。未完成的写明原因，需要支持的说清具体事项。发送前去掉重复内容并核对日期，能节省团队时间。

title: An evening walk
en: The streets are quieter after my late shift. On some evenings, I take a short walk before going home. I leave my headphones in my bag and listen to the city around me. A shop is closing, a bus is arriving, and someone is walking a dog. These ordinary moments help me slow down. When I reach home, I feel ready to put work aside. The day has been busy, but it can end gently.
cn: 夜班后街上安静了，我有时散步回家，不戴耳机，听商店打烊、公交进站和遛狗人的声音。这些普通瞬间让我慢下来，准备把工作暂时放下。

title: Working together
en: During rehearsal, our team tried a new arrangement. At first, two people were standing too close to the camera. Instead of blaming anyone, we stopped and looked at the screen together. Each person suggested one small change. After a few minutes, everyone could be seen clearly. The result was better because we listened to each other. We also wrote down the final positions, so the next rehearsal could begin with less confusion.
cn: 排练时两个人离相机太近。我们一起看屏幕、各提一个小改动，最后每个人都能清晰入镜。相互倾听改善了效果，记下站位也让下次排练更省事。

title: A place for everything
en: My bag used to be full of loose cables, tickets, and small notes. I often spent several minutes looking for one thing. One weekend, I gave each type of item its own place. Cables went into a small pocket, and receipts went into a separate envelope. I put important notes on my phone instead of leaving them on paper. My bag is still busy, but finding what I need is much easier now.
cn: 以前包里散放着线材、票据和便签，找东西很费时间。后来我给每类物品固定位置：线材装小袋，票据放信封，重要笔记记到手机里。

title: Trying a new word
en: Today I learned the word prepare. I had seen it before, but I rarely used it myself. I made a short sentence about work and said it aloud several times. Then I changed the sentence to describe tomorrow. This helped me practise the meaning and the sound together. I may forget the word later, and that is all right. When it appears again, I will have a real memory to connect it with.
cn: 今天我学了 prepare，用工作场景造句，朗读后又改成描述明天的句子，同时练习词义和发音。即使以后忘了，再见到它时也有真实记忆可以联系。

title: A change of plans
en: We planned to record a short video outside, but it started raining in the afternoon. The team moved the equipment indoors and chose a quieter corner of the studio. We changed the lighting and tested a new camera angle. The setting was different, but the main idea still worked. After recording, we saved a note about the change. Next time we plan an outdoor session, we will prepare an indoor option as well.
cn: 原定户外录制遇到下雨，团队转到室内，重新调整灯光和角度，主要创意仍然可用。记录这次变化后，下次安排户外工作时也会准备室内方案。

title: Looking at progress
en: It is easy to forget small improvements when you look only at the final goal. At the end of each week, I open my records and look for one useful change. Perhaps I finished a task earlier or remembered a difficult English word. Sometimes the week was simply more consistent than the last one. I write down what helped and keep that habit. Progress is easier to understand when I compare real days instead of imagined perfect ones.
cn: 只盯最终目标很容易忘记小进步。每周我查看真实记录，找一件有改善的事，记下有效的方法。与真实的过去比较，比和想象中的完美状态比较更容易理解进展。

title: A quiet morning
en: I do not start every day at the same time. After a late shift, my morning may begin when other people are eating lunch. I open the curtains, drink some water, and check my plan. I choose a few things that fit the time and energy I have. There is no need to copy someone else's schedule exactly. A useful routine should help me live my own day, even when that day begins later.
cn: 我每天起床时间不固定，夜班后的早晨可能已是别人的午饭时间。我拉开窗帘、喝水、看计划，按自己的时间和精力选择事项，让作息服务于自己的生活。

title: Saving a backup
en: A friend once lost a notebook full of useful records. The experience reminded me to make a backup of my own work. Now I save a copy before changing devices or clearing old files. I give the file a clear name with the date and keep it somewhere I can find again. I also check that the copy opens correctly. A backup is most helpful when I know what it contains and how to use it.
cn: 朋友丢失笔记的经历提醒我备份。换设备或清文件前，我保存一份带日期的副本，放到容易找的位置，并检查能否打开，确认里面有什么、怎样恢复。

title: Asking for help
en: During a meeting, I did not understand the last instruction. For a moment, I wanted to stay quiet and guess what it meant. Then I asked the speaker to explain it again with an example. The example made the task much clearer, and another teammate said it helped them too. Asking a short question took less time than fixing a mistake later. I wrote down the answer so I could use it after the meeting.
cn: 会议里我没听懂最后一条指示，原想猜一猜，后来请对方举例解释。例子也帮到了其他同事。及时提问比事后返工更省时间，我还记下答案方便会后使用。

title: Choosing the next task
en: My task list sometimes becomes longer than I expected. When that happens, I stop adding new items for a moment. I check which task has a real deadline and which one can wait. Then I choose a single task to begin. Finishing it does not solve everything, but it makes the list feel more manageable. Before moving on, I decide whether the next task still matters. A plan can change as the day changes.
cn: 任务比预计多时，我先停下来，分清真正有截止日期的事项与可以等的事项，再选一件开始。每完成一件都重新看下一项是否重要，计划可以随一天的变化调整。

title: Recording a sentence
en: When I practise speaking, I sometimes record one short sentence on my phone. I listen to the example first and notice where the speaker pauses. Then I make my own recording and play it back. I choose just one thing to improve, such as a final sound or a longer pause. I do not expect the first recording to be perfect. The second try often sounds clearer because I know what to listen for.
cn: 练口语时，我先听例句的停顿，再录下自己的版本回放，每次只改善一个细节，例如尾音或停顿。不要求第一次完美，知道关注什么后，第二次往往会更清楚。

title: After the performance
en: The performance is over, but our work is not quite finished. We check that all files are saved and put the equipment back in its place. Each person shares one thing that went well and one thing to improve. We keep the discussion short because everyone is tired. Before leaving, we confirm the next meeting time. This small closing routine helps us finish the day clearly and begin the next session with less uncertainty.
cn: 演出后还要确认文件保存、设备归位。大家简短分享一件做得好的事和一件待改进的事，再确认下次集合时间。这套收尾步骤让当天结束得更清楚。

title: A steady habit
en: I used to restart my learning plan whenever I missed a day. I would choose too many tasks and feel disappointed when I could not finish them. Now I return to the next small lesson instead of starting everything again. I review a few words and read a short passage. The record shows both busy days and quiet days. I am learning to build a habit that can survive a changing schedule, rather than a perfect week that never happens.
cn: 以前漏学一天就重启计划、安排过多任务，然后失望。现在直接回到下一小节，复习几个词、读短文，让习惯适应不固定的作息，而不追求永远完美的一周。
